Quantile regression for panel data with individual effects

Source: R/panqr.R
panqr.Rd

Fixed-effects quantile regression for linear panel models: the two-step estimator of Canay (2011) and the method of moments quantile regression (MM-QR) of Machado and Santos Silva (2019), the estimator of the Stata command xtqreg. A pooled quantile regression that ignores the individual effects is available as a baseline. Several quantiles can be estimated in one call.

Usage

panqr(
  formula,
  data,
  index,
  tau = 0.5,
  model = c("canay", "mmqr", "pooling"),
  vcov = NULL,
  boot = 200,
  na.action = stats::na.omit,
  seed = NULL,
  R,
  cluster = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

a formula y ~ regressors. lag(x, k), lead(x, k) and diff(x) are taken within each individual on the grid of sorted distinct time values (see "Lags and differences" in panglm(); needs index = c(id, time)); the first waves of each individual get NA and leave the sample, and lag(x, 0:2) gives several lags

data

a data.frame in long format

index

length-1 or length-2 character vector giving the individual (and time) columns

tau

numeric vector of quantiles, each strictly between 0 and 1

model

"canay", "mmqr" or "pooling"

vcov

"analytic" (cluster-robust), "iid" (MM-QR only), "bootstrap" or "none"; the default is "bootstrap" for "canay" and "analytic" otherwise

boot

number of bootstrap replications for vcov = "bootstrap"

na.action

missing-data action passed to stats::model.frame()

seed

optional random seed for the bootstrap; the global random number state is restored afterwards. With seed = NULL (the default) the draws come from the global random number stream.

R

deprecated; use boot

cluster

optional name of a column of data to cluster the analytic covariance on (vcov = "analytic" only, including the MM-QR location and scale covariances); the default clusters by individual

Value

an object of class "panqr", a list with components coefficients (a matrix with one column per quantile), vcov (a list of covariance matrices, one per quantile, or NULL for vcov = "none"), vcov_type, tau, model, boot (the bootstrap replicates, an array boot x k x length(tau), for vcov = "bootstrap"), alpha (one per individual: for "canay" the normalized effects subtracted from the outcome, for "mmqr" the location effects including the constant), for "mmqr" also location, scale (lists with coefficients and vcov), q (the quantiles of the standardized errors) and delta (the individual scale effects including the constant, so that alpha_i(tau) = alpha_i + delta_i q(tau)), cluster and n_clusters (for the analytic covariances), dropped (time-invariant regressors dropped), n_singletons (individuals observed once, dropped for "canay" and "mmqr"), nobs, n_groups, call and formula. Methods: print, summary, coef, vcov, confint, nobs, plot, tidy and glance.

Estimators

  • "canay": the individual effects are estimated from the within (mean) regression, alpha_i = ybar_i - xbar_i'b - c with c = ybar - xbar'b the overall constant (the normalization of Stata's xtreg, fe), and the quantile regression of the adjusted outcome y - alpha_i on the regressors (with an intercept) is fitted by quantreg::rq.fit() with method = "br". The intercept is the tau-quantile of c + error. The model assumes that the individual effects are pure location shifts, and the estimator is consistent when both N and T grow.

  • "mmqr": the location-scale model y_it = alpha_i + x_it'b + (delta_i + x_it'g) U_it. The location parameters b come from the within regression of y on x; with R its residuals, the scale parameters g come from the within regression of 2 R (I(R >= 0) - mean(I(R >= 0))), an estimate of |R| that is robust to the first step; q(tau) is the sample tau-quantile of the standardized residuals R / sigma_it, with sigma_it the fitted scale including the individual effects. The quantile coefficients are b(tau) = b + g q(tau). The scale variables are the regressors, as in xtqreg. Only slopes are reported: the intercept is absorbed in the individual effects alpha_i(tau) = alpha_i + delta_i q(tau).

  • "pooling": quantreg::rq.fit() of y on the regressors, ignoring the panel structure (except for the clustered covariance).

Time-invariant regressors are not identified with individual effects and are dropped (with a warning) for "canay" and "mmqr", as are individuals observed only once (with a message).

Covariance

vcov = "bootstrap" resamples whole individuals with replacement (a cluster bootstrap) boot times, repeats every step of the estimator and returns the covariance of the replicates. vcov = "analytic" gives:

  • "mmqr": a cluster-robust (by individual, or by cluster) sandwich built from the influence function of b(tau) = b + g q(tau). The influence of observation it adds the three steps of the estimator: the location within regression, Q^{-1} x~_it R_it; the scale within regression, q(tau) Q^{-1} x~_it sigma_it V_it; and the quantile q(tau), g s_i w_it / sum(s), with Q = sum x~ x~', s_i the scale of individual i at the regressor means and w_it = (tau - I(U_it <= q(tau))) / f(q(tau)) - U_it - q(tau) V_it. These are summed within clusters into psi_g, and V = G / (G - 1) * sum_g psi_g psi_g' for G clusters. The density of the standardized error at q(tau) is the difference quotient 2h / (q(tau + h) - q(tau - h)) (as Stata's qreg, vce(iid)) with the Hall and Sheather bandwidth h. The scale influence uses the centered V = 2 U (I(U >= 0) - mean(I(U >= 0))) - 1 of the paper (also used by the Stata command mmqreg). Unlike the iid formula, it allows the errors of an individual to be dependent (serial correlation, or an individual component in U) and the errors to be heteroskedastic.

vcov = "iid" (MM-QR only) gives the asymptotic covariance of Machado and Santos Silva (2019) under independent observations, with the matrix layout of xtqreg (version 1.5) and the same density estimate and centered V; xtqreg 1.5 omits the - 1 in V, which inflates its standard errors away from the median. This was the analytic covariance of "mmqr" before panglm 1.6.1. It replaces observation-level products by their sample means and ignores the dependence within individuals; it can be far off with short panels (see the package's validation suite).

The other models with vcov = "analytic":

  • "canay": a cluster-robust (by individual) sandwich built from the influence function of the two-step estimator, which corrects the quantile regression score (tau - I(e < 0)) x for the estimation of the individual effects and of the within slopes. The conditional density is estimated with the Gaussian kernel and bandwidth of quantreg::summary.rq(se = "ker"). This is a large-N, large-T approximation; Canay (2011) recommends the bootstrap. It treats the individual effects as fixed, so its intercept SE omits the sampling variation of the mean individual effect that the cluster bootstrap includes; the slope SEs of the two agree.

  • "pooling": the same kernel sandwich without the first-step terms, clustered by individual.

The "canay" and "pooling" cluster sandwiches carry no finite-sample factor; the "mmqr" one carries G / (G - 1). For "mmqr" the location and scale coefficients are returned with the cluster-robust within covariance of the rest of the package (G / (G - 1) * (n - 1) / (n - k), as plm::vcovHC(type = "sss")).

Validation

Numerical accuracy is checked in the package tests and in the validation suite; see the validation article on the package website.

References

Canay, I. A. (2011). A simple approach to quantile regression for panel data. The Econometrics Journal, 14(3), 368-386. doi:10.1111/j.1368-423X.2011.00349.x

Machado, J. A. F. and Santos Silva, J. M. C. (2019). Quantiles via moments. Journal of Econometrics, 213(1), 145-173. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2019.04.009

See also

summary.panqr(), vcov.panqr() and plot.panqr() for the fitted model, tidy-methods for tidy() and glance().

Other panel models: panfmm(), panfmmselect(), panglm(), pangmm(), panhurdle(), paniv(), panselect(), twopart()

Examples

# Simulated panel of 300 patients over 6 years. Annual health costs have
# a patient effect and a heavy upper tail that widens with chronic
# conditions: a location-scale model in which the effect of chronic
# conditions grows across the cost distribution.
set.seed(1)
N <- 300; TT <- 6
d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), year = rep(seq_len(TT), N))
alpha <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT)
d$chronic <- rpois(N * TT, 1 + 0.5 * (alpha > 0))
d$age <- rep(sample(40:70, N, TRUE), each = TT) + d$year
d$cost <- 2 + alpha + 0.5 * d$chronic + 0.02 * d$age +
  (1 + 0.3 * d$chronic) * rexp(N * TT)

if (requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # median and upper tail of costs, MM-QR with analytic standard errors
  mm <- panqr(cost ~ chronic + age, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),
              tau = c(0.5, 0.9), model = "mmqr")
  summary(mm)

  # Canay two-step estimator with a small cluster bootstrap
  cn <- panqr(cost ~ chronic + age, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),
              tau = 0.9, model = "canay", boot = 50, seed = 1)
  coef(cn)
}
#> Warning: 0.1% of the fitted values of the scale function are not positive
#> Warning: Solution may be nonunique
#> Warning: Solution may be nonunique
#> (Intercept)     chronic         age 
#>  4.11072454  1.19437845  0.02214631
